n: The date is precise: late summer of 520 BC, under the Persian king Darius I. The Jews had returned from Babylon about 18 years earlier, but the temple still lay unfinished. Haggai speaks to the governor and high priest.

f.g: Darius I of Persia, who reigned 522–486 BC.
Governor of Judah, a grandson of King Jehoiachin — a descendant of David.
The high priest, also called Jeshua (Ezra 3:2).

n: The people were saying, “It’s not the right time to build the Lord’s house.” Opposition and hard times had stalled the work since about 536 BC.
God’s answer comes through His prophet.
A pointed question: Is it time for you to live in nicely paneled houses while My house lies in ruins? Their priorities were upside down.

f.g: Paneled houses — finished with fine wood, a sign of comfort.

n: “Consider your ways” — think carefully about what you’re doing and what it’s producing. Haggai repeats this call several times.

f.g: Literally “set your heart on your ways.”

n: They work hard but never get ahead: big plantings, small harvests; never enough food or warmth; wages leaking out like coins from a bag with holes. Neglecting God left them empty.

f.w: Ye have sown much, and bring in little

n: Again God urges them to reflect honestly on their choices.
The solution is simple: go to the hills, bring timber, and build. God will be pleased and glorified in it.
They hoped for much but got little, and God blew it away. Why? Because they rushed to their own houses while His lay in ruins.

f.w: ye run every man unto his own house

n: That’s why the sky has held back dew and the land its crops. The drought was a message.

f.g: Withheld dew — vital moisture in Israel’s dry summers.

n: God called a drought on grain, wine, oil, people, animals, and all their work. Everything they depended on suffered.

f.g: Hebrew ḥoreb — a wordplay with ḥareb, “waste” (v. 4, 9): a wasted house brings a dry land.

n: The leaders and the people obeyed the Lord’s voice through Haggai, and they reverenced the Lord. A rare and quick response to a prophet!

f.w: obeyed the voice of the LORD

f.g: Those who had returned from exile.

n: Haggai, the Lord’s messenger, brings a short but powerful promise: “I am with you.”
The Lord stirred up the spirit of the governor, high priest, and people, and they began working on the temple. God gives energy to those who obey.

f.w: the LORD stirred up the spirit

n: Work began just 23 days after Haggai’s first message — September 520 BC. Obedience was swift.

f.w: the four and twentieth day of the sixth month
